The petitioner is the accused in SC No. 1137 of 2022 on the file of the Additional District and Sessions Court (for the trial of cases relating to atrocities and sexual violence towards women and children), Kozhikode arising out of Crime No. 117 of 2019 of Medical College Police Station.

The offences alleged against the petitioner are under Sections 450,
376(n) and 420 IPC.

The prosecution case is that the petitioner after promising to marry the defacto complainant, had sexual intercourse with her and also received more than Rs. 38 lakhs from her and thereafter he failed to marry her and thereby he alleged to have committed the aforesaid offences.

2. According to the learned Counsel for the petitioner even as per the allegations in the final report,
the relationship between the petitioner and the defacto complainant was only a consensual one and as such no offence is made out against him.
Therefore he prayed for quashing all further proceedings against him.
3. The petition was strongly opposed by the learned Public Prosecutor.
From the FI statement itself it is revealed that the petitioner and the defacto complainant became friends since 2015.
It is alleged that on one day in April 2018, he came to the bedroom of her house and had sexual intercourse with her without her consent.
According to her, the petitioner promised to marry her.
Thereafter, she accompanied him to various places including Dubai, Kodaikkanal and other places and had sexual intercourse with each other.
In the meantime, some money transactions were also there.
It is also stated that, in 2018 alone she came to know that the petitioner was already married.
Even then she continued her relationship with the petitioner, accompanied him to various places and had sexual intercourse with him.

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, from the available evidence it is clear that the relationship between the petitioner and the defacto complainant was a consensual one.

Since the petitioner was married at the time of the relationship between the petitioner and the defacto complainant and she continued the relationship even after she came to know that he was a married man, her claim that,
she had given consent as the petitioner promised to marry 2025:KER:83843 her cannot be believed.
Though it is alleged that the petitioner received more than Rs. 38 lakhs from him, prima facie it is a loan transaction and as such the offence under Section 420 IPC also is not attracted.
Therefore continuation of the proceedings against the petitioner further will only be an abuse of the process of court.
In the result, this Crl.M.C is allowed.

All further proceedings against the petitioner in SC No. 1137 of 2022 on the file of the Additional District and Sessions Court (for the trial of cases relating to atrocities and sexual violence towards women and children), Kozhikode, arising from crime No.117 of 2019 of Medical College Police Station, stands quashed under section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
